records.real_world_identity_notes: McLaren 720S GT3 of 2019, running a race-prepared version of the McLaren M840T 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 through a six-speed sequential paddle gearbox with an electronic shift actuator. It is the model that preceded the 720S GT3 Evo, which AMS2 curates separately in its own class.
records.confidence_basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by a registered source.
records.identity_basis: A registered source establishes the 2019 720S GT3 and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
records.specification_basis: The source gives a six-speed sequential paddle gearbox, and the live drive selected six paddle gears with automatic cut and blip and no clutch needed to pull away.
records.confidence_notes: Guided testing directly established the six paddle gears, the clutch-free move-off, the clutchless running shifts, and automatic cut and blip.
control_notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: clutch-free move-off, automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies none of the three.

This is a different car from the curated McLaren 720S GT3 Evo. AMS2 places this one in the GT3 class and the Evo in GT3_Gen2, and nothing is inherited between them even though both are six-speed paddle cars.
Only the plain identity has been observed for this car and its class has reported no aero package, so no further identity is carried.
